articles.title: France slams Israel’s ‘demagogic’ ban on opposition leader Melenchon
articles.summary: Israel’s move came after France banned a prominent Israeli settler from entering the country.
articles.body:
Paris has condemned Israel’s “demagogic decision” to bar French opposition figure Jean-Luc Melenchon from entering the country.

Late on Thursday, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot slammed Israel’s earlier announcement that Melenchon, leader of the France Unbowed party (La France Insoumise), was not welcome.

Israel barred the party’s parliamentary group chair Mathilde Panot, alongside Melenchon, due to the “extreme anti-Israel stance” of the party and “outrageous statements” made by its leaders.

“This demagogic decision, coming from a government that has repeatedly violated international law, plays into the hands of those who, like La France Insoumise, make a living out of exploiting the Israeli-Palestinian conflict,” Barrot, who belongs to the centrist ruling coalition, wrote on social media.

“France will continue tirelessly to work toward a two-state solution and peaceful coexistence between the Israeli and Palestinian peoples,” the minister added.

Israel accused Melenchon and Panot of making “blood libel” statements against Israel.

At the weekend, Melenchon had said that if he was victorious in the upcoming presidential election in April 2027, he would order French ships to escort flotillas taking aid to Gaza.

The Israeli military has previously raided such fleets and detained activists.

“Israel will respond firmly to those who seek to harm it and will not allow individuals who act against Israel and incite against its citizens to enter the country,” a statement from the Israeli Foreign Ministry said.

Speaking to French radio, Melenchon said that he had been “banned from entering a territory I did not ask to enter”.

The Israeli move came after France barred a prominent Israeli settler last week.

Yossi Dagan, a member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party, who heads one of six Israeli regional councils in the occupied West Bank, was denied permission to enter France after landing at Charles de Gaulle International Airport.

France’s Foreign Ministry confirmed that Dagan was barred “due to his active role in implementing Israel’s settlement policy,” which violates international law.

France was one of several European countries this year to step up restrictions on Israeli settlers, spurring outrage from Israeli officials.

Earlier this year, France banned far-right Israeli ministers, Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, who are both members of Netanyahu’s cabinet and have encouraged accelerated settlement in the West Bank and pogroms targeting Palestinians.

articles.title: Kenyan building collapse near Nairobi kills six people
articles.summary: Five people reportedly survive as emergency crews search for anyone still trapped in the rubble.
articles.body:
The collapse of an unfinished eight-storey building in Kenya has killed six people.

The structure fell on Friday morning in Syokimau on the outskirts of Nairobi. Coming on the heels of a similar recent incident in the capital, the accident has revived calls for stronger safety oversight.

Construction workers were reportedly at the site when the building’s uppermost concrete slab gave way, bringing down part of the structure, according to a preliminary report from Nairobi City County’s emergency team. The report did not establish why the slab failed.

The Kenya Red Cross initially reported that three people had been rescued and one person was reported missing. TV reports later said that five people had been pulled alive from the rubble and taken to hospital.

The emergency report said the number of workers present when the building fell had not been confirmed, leaving open the possibility that others were trapped.

Firefighters and specialist rescue teams were continuing to search for survivors.

Patrick Makau, a member of Kenya’s parliament representing Mavoko, the constituency that includes Syokimau, urged rescue agencies in a post on social media to act quickly.

“Every second counts,” he wrote, offering condolences to the victims’ families.

The accident follows a similar deadly building collapse in the city on October 23, which killed eight people. The twin disasters have prompted calls for tougher construction oversight.

The Kenya Institute for Public Policy Research and Analysis, a state research body, has identified poor workmanship, inadequate supervision, substandard materials and faulty designs as wider causes of building collapses.

articles.title: Hunt for clues in deadly Brooklyn building collapse will take time
articles.summary: Investigators began what could be a long search for the cause of a Brooklyn apartment building collapse that killed eight people as the fire department ended rescue operations Thursday after the last victim was freed from the wreckage.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Investigators began what could be a long search for the cause of a Brooklyn apartment building collapse that killed eight people as the fire department ended rescue operations Thursday after the last victim was freed from the wreckage. The three-story building gave way while construction workers were digging Wednesday afternoon at an adjacent lot, causing New York City’s mayor to order inspections at about 100 building sites involving companies related to the project. “If there is anyone, or any entity, operating in this city that bears responsibility for what happened, we will hold them fully accountable,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani said during a news conference. Investigators have not determined what caused the collapse. Two children, ages 9 and 10, were killed along with adults ranging in age from 22 to 31, according to the New York City Police Department. There were also 18 injured, including four firefighters, Mamdani said. The children were Colombian, as was one of the adults who was killed, according to the country’s consulate in New York. One witness said he watched bricks fall minutes before the disaster while a woman in a neighboring building said she and fellow residents blamed vibrations from the construction for cracks that appeared in their apartment walls. Emergency workers used power saws and pickaxes to get through the debris, pulling four victims out of the rubble in the early hours of Thursday. Hours later, excavators removed larger chunks of the wreckage so searchers could get deeper into the construction pit, said New York Fire Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore. Witnesses describe the aftermath and destruction James Williams, who works at a deli across the street, said he heard loud banging at the site all day Wednesday and looked outside to see bricks falling. “Two minutes later, the building collapsed,” he said. As the building crumbled and exposed the neighboring building, Williams spotted a woman on a staircase. “There wasn’t anything I could do,” he said, his voice cracking. Customers and stylists at a nearby hair salon jumped up and ran onto the sidewalk as the building fell. “We heard the boom and we all rushed outside and saw smoke and dust everywhere,” said hairstylist Brigitte Anama. She saw emergency workers pulling people from the rubble, including what appeared to be a child. “People were saying, ‘Pray for the baby, pray for the baby,’” Anama said. Dervie Mapp, who lives along the construction site, said she and others complained for months about the project. Her landlord brought engineers into the building, but residents never received an inspection report, she said. Determining cause of Brooklyn collapse will take time, expert says Construction safety expert Glenn Corbett of John Jay College in New York said it’s way too early to know what caused the accident. “It could be a design flaw, it could be a construction flaw, or it could be some kind of work that was going on,” he said. It appeared that the shoring of the excavation work failed, but finding out why will take more investigating, he said. The one-story building previously on the site was demolished earlier this year. Records show a contractor, Mordechai “Marty” Waisbrod, notified the city that excavation would begin in September and include rock blasting. Permit applications indicated plans to dig below 15 feet (4.5 meters). Phone and email messages were left at one of Waisbrod’s Brooklyn-based businesses. Engineering drawings submitted with the applications show various plans to brace walls at the edge of the site. Messages were left Thursday for the engineer, Jieming Wang, and for an inspector who’s listed as being involved with the project. Rescuers faced a massive pile of rubble This was the second high-profile structural problem with a building in New York in the past five months. In July, several buildings in Manhattan were evacuated after support columns buckled inside a skyscraper that once was the headquarters of Pfizer. First responders in Brooklyn worked to clear a massive heap that included mattresses, a broken sink and a refrigerator tossed on its side. Scattered in the debris were vinyl records, clothes and shoes. Firefighters pulled a pregnant woman from the rubble Wednesday, hoisted her up on a stretcher and rushed her to a waiting ambulance. Others were rescued as the night wore on. Building records show there were four apartments on the upper two floors and a commercial unit on the ground floor of the collapsed building. Victims were from multiple countries The police department identified those killed as Nicole Daniela Salvada Rodriguez, 9; Juan Daniel Salvada Guzman, 31; Kevin Santiago Reyes Gonzalez, 10; Ndiaye Mamadou, 31; Barry Mamadou, 23; Gabriel Siguencia, 22; Edgar Sapon, 26; and Jose Luis Caguana Cosquillo, 26. Some of the victims were from Mexico, Colombia, Ecuador and Trinidad, New York’s mayor said. Two of the dead were construction workers, he said. Some workers who survived joined firefighters in digging out survivors, he said. Caguana Cosquillo and Siguencia were from Ecuador, according to the Consulate of Ecuador in New York. Carlos Caguana said his brother, José, was working at the construction site and had a pregnant wife and a young child. “He was the sole provider for the family,” Caguana told WNBC-TV. The surrounding blocks along Flatbush Avenue, a busy thoroughfare in Brooklyn, are tightly packed with older brick buildings and a few newly built apartment complexes. A mix of Caribbean and Mexican restaurants reflects the diversity of the neighborhood. Inspectors reported violations earlier this year New York City’s buildings commissioner, Ahmed Tigani, said Wednesday that construction workers were excavating the empty lot next door when the building buckled. The city’s Department of Buildings is investigating. City officials said a stop work order was issued in March after inspectors concluded the building next door was being demolished without adequate overhead protection such as netting to shield neighboring buildings, the department said in an emailed statement. In April, inspectors found that the demolition work had resumed in violation of the stop work order, the department said. Work was allowed to continue after the problems were corrected, it said.

articles.title: Shetland cruise ship numbers hit record levels
articles.summary: Nearly a million tonnes of seabed have been removed from waters around Lerwick to improve access.
articles.body:
The number of cruise ships visiting Lerwick harbour has reached record levels.

Some 137 cruise vessels docked between April and October, bringing more than 122,000 passengers to Shetland.

Nearly a million tonnes of seabed have been removed from waters around Lerwick to improve access for large cruise ships.

Lerwick Port Authority (LPA) described the season as a "significant milestone" and said the completion of a £25m dredging project would allow larger vessels to berth next year.

A harbour spokesperson said 2026 had been its "busiest" year yet, with first time visits from a range of luxury brands.

Lerwick is an increasingly popular destination for international cruise operators, partly credited to the success of BBC One TV crime drama Shetland .

The industry is a core part of the local economy but it is considerably smaller than in Orkney, where 223 vessels visited Kirkwall in 2024.

Melanie Henderson, the port authority's cruise and marketing manager, said it had been an impressive season with many local businesses and organisations playing their part.

The harbour said cruise bookings now extended until 2035, with a focus on developing a sustainable programme.

The largest cruise ships are typically anchored off Lerwick, with passengers brought to shore in small shuttle boats.

The harbour said the completion of a £25m dredging project in October would strengthen its ability to accommodate bigger vessels.

Capt Calum Grains, chief executive of LPA, said it had been its "single biggest project" to date and would support other sectors like fishing, aquaculture and energy.

More stories from North East Scotland, Orkney and Shetland

Listen to news from North East Scotland on BBC Sounds

Specialist contractor Boskalis Westminster finished the capital dredging project last month.

The complex operation involved explosives to crack underwater rocks with all of the material shipped to an offshore disposal site.

Grains said it had been challenging because of environmental considerations but it had been done using high-tech equipment in order to have the "lowest impact".

Lerwick has also seen strong numbers using its tourist office with 82,000 people visiting since it reopened in April.

The Shetland tourism association stepped in to save the shop after national agency Visit Scotland moved its services online.

Association chair Amanda Hawick said 74 crafters were trading through the new office with "a list of more creatives waiting to come onboard".

articles.title: “Welcome home”: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg surprises his mother with a California house after she helped him return to basketball in high school
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg expresses gratitude to his mother by surprising her with a new house in California, acknowledging her vital support in his basketball journey.
articles.body: Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has begun his NBA career after years of hard work, but he has not forgotten the person who helped him get there. His mother, Yissel Raposo, stood by him during a difficult period in high school and pushed him to get his education back on track, so he could continue playing basketball. Now, Lendeborg has found a special way to thank her for that support by surprising her with a new home in California. As he handed her the keys, he said, “Welcome home.” According to ESPN’s Anthony Gharib, Lendeborg shared the moment in a YouTube video titled “This one’s for Mama Yax,” where Raposo appeared teary-eyed as she opened the door of the house with her son.Yaxel Lendeborg surprised his mother with a new California homeAs noted by ABC News, he announced his excitement about purchasing the house in a video posted on his YouTube channel titled “This one’s for Mama Yax.” He revealed that the purchase of the house was one of his personal ambitions and that it took him 2 to 3 months. He made sure that his relatives and friends assembled outside the property first before he showed his mother into the house. He presented his mother with a gift box that contained the keys to the house.His mother opened the gift box, took out the keys and walked into the house with her son. It was also a significant change for Raposo as she was getting ready to move from New Jersey to California to be near her son. According to ESPN, Lendeborg posted the video on his YouTube channel on November 6, 2026. “There is no gesture big enough to properly say thank you for all the love, sacrifice, and support my mom has poured into me but this moment was pretty special and one I’ll never forget,” he wrote. He added that the moment meant more to him than basketball because he wanted the people who believed in him to enjoy the success.His mother helped him return to basketball during high schoolThis gesture is special in relation to Raposo because she has contributed significantly to altering the trajectory of her son's life. As per The Players’ Tribune, in his essay written in February 2026 and titled "My Mom Saved My Life", Lendeborg described how he had struggled with academics as a senior in high school in 2019. He spent most of his time playing video games, sleeping in class and was not eligible for basketball due to his academic performance. However, in a discussion in her minivan, she challenged him by demanding that he finish 10 courses at a local community college in one year to graduate. Though he had been reluctant at first, he completed the courses and became eligible to play basketball. He went on to get into a basketball showcase for Dominican players near New York, after which his mother managed to get him an opportunity at Arizona Western College in Yuma, Arizona.The Warriors rookie reached the NBA after years of college basketballAccording to ESPN, Lendeborg played three seasons at Arizona Western College, a community college in Yuma and two at UAB before transferring to Michigan as a graduate student in 2025. Lendeborg helped lead Michigan to the national title, according to ESPN and he was also named Big Ten Player of the Year and a First-Team All-American.The Philadelphia Inquirer reported that the Golden State Warriors picked Lendeborg in the 11th spot during the 2026 NBA draft on June 23. This progression from junior college basketball to the NBA became an emotional experience for Raposo, as she embraced her son following his selection. KAWC reported on June 24, 2026, that Lendeborg, who played at Arizona Western College from 2020 to 2023, became the fifth player from the program to reach the NBA.You use AI every day. articles.title: German spies handed new powers to tackle 'hybrid threats' from abroad
articles.summary: German reforms mean foreign and domestic intelligence services will have greater powers to combat espionage, terrorism and sabotage.
articles.body:
Germany's foreign and domestic intelligence services are to be given greater powers to combat espionage, terrorism and sabotage after the country's parliament, the Bundestag, approved a major overhaul of its legislation.

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, who championed the bill, has called it a "reform of the century", necessary because of the increasing threats from foreign powers.

But the Left Party's security spokeswoman, Clara Bünger, said Dobrindt was creating a new German secret police.

The legislation gives numerous new powers to Germany's BND federal intelligence service, and its BfV domestic service, the Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution.

In the Bundestag, 309 MPs voted in favour of the new law on intelligence services, while 190 voted against and 71 abstained.

For historical reasons, German intelligence has mainly focused on gathering information rather than acting on it.

In future, German spies working for the BND, which is responsible for foreign intelligence, will be able to conduct covert operations abroad, including sabotage.

This could include paralysing the servers of state-sponsored hacker groups, disrupting disinformation networks, or even disrupting supply chains for weapons.

Agents for the domestic intelligence service, the BfV, will no longer to be limited to gathering information. For the first time they will be able to take protective action against property and IT systems, if specific threats are identified.

That means they will be allowed to dismantle or break explosives or weapons, divert or block data flows during cyber-attacks, delete or falsify data stored for malicious purposes, and plant false information on those involved.

Germany target of 'intensive' espionage, Merz says after suspected Russian spy arrest

Sabotage suspect held in Germany after spate of attacks on power grid

Germany says Russia behind Leipzig airport drone attack

Under certain conditions, BfV agents will also be permitted to enter homes covertly. However, the measure must always be authorised in advance.

They will also be given wider powers of digital surveillance, including monitoring encrypted telecommunications and carrying out online searches. They will also be allowed to use AI-supported data analysis and biometric image matching on the internet.

The government says the reform is needed because of an increase in foreign espionage, particularly from Russia, China and Iran.

"We are the target of hybrid threats," said Dobrindt. "Germany is a theatre of operations for terrorism, extremism and foreign powers."

In August, a drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at Leipzig Airport, close to Ukrainian cargo planes. However, it failed to explode as the bomb's detonator was apparently faulty.

German authorities say Russia was behind the attack.

The new law has been bitterly criticised by some opposition politicians, even though Dobrindt has said it is "madness" to think it means that Germany is creating a new secret police.

And Clara Bünger from the Left Party told public broadcaster ARD that the new law was "a monster… summoning ghosts that we will probably never be able to get rid of".

The separation between the police and the secret service, she warned, was "being eroded" - and Bünger said that had been a lesson learned from the Nazi era.

"This means the secret service is being granted executive powers and will not only be allowed to act pre-emptively, but will also be granted police powers."

However, Sonja Eichwede of the centre-left SPD, which is part of Germany's governing coalition, said the reforms would make a significant contribution to ensuring the country's democracy was "robust and resilient".

articles.title: Turkiye and Qatar sign mutual defence agreement
articles.summary: The pact was signed after the President met Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim ‌bin Hamad Al Thani in Istanbul on ⁠Friday.
articles.body:
Turkiye and ⁠Qatar have signed a mutual defence agreement after a meeting between Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan and Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim ‌bin Hamad Al Thani in Istanbul on Friday.

“President Erdogan stated that we would continue working together to prevent ⁠the resurgence of ⁠war in the Gulf region and establish a basis ⁠for dialogue and ⁠achieve peace,” ⁠the Turkish presidency said in a statement on X.

Erdogan’s office said the agreement would “add a new dimension to relations between Turkiye and Qatar”, while the Qatari Emir praised the deal as a “strategic partnership.”

In a post on X, Sheikh Tamim wrote that he “discussed ways to build on what has been achieved and identify priorities for joint action in the coming period” during talks the with President Erdogan.

A statement by the Amiri Diwan said multiple agreements were signed by the two governments, including a memorandum of understanding “on cooperation in the field of peace, reconciliation and conflict resolution”.

Speaking to Al Jazeera, security analyst Yusuf Alabarda said that since the start of the Iran war, countries in the region “are feeling the effects of the war and no one is feeling secure”.

“All the Gulf countries, but especially Qatar, understood that their security guarantees from the United States are not working properly. The Turkish troops in Qatar are very important but I can say that in the near term Turkish weapons and air defences might be deployed to Qatar to guarantee its safety, which is very important to Turkiye, so this agreement will help move forward these military deals,” Alabarda said.

In August, Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed a regional defence pact under which the three countries would come to each other’s aid if one of them was attacked.

Ratified by the Turkish parliament last week, the pact links NATO member Turkiye, which has the alliance’s second-largest military, with Pakistan, the Muslim world’s only nuclear-armed state, and Saudi Arabia.

Turkiye has said the agreement is not aimed at any other country and remains open to other states, including Egypt.

In October, Qatar, Indonesia, Pakistan and Turkiye signed a multilateral memorandum of understanding on defence cooperation in Doha.

The agreement, known as “Badr”, aims to bolster cooperation between the participating countries.

articles.title: Police investigating David Walliams over reports alleging serious sexual offences
articles.summary: The Met Police said the allegations are separate from those reported by ITV and the Guardian earlier this week.
articles.body:
The Metropolitan Police has launched an investigation into David Walliams over reports of "alleged serious sexual offences".

It comes after ITV News and the Guardian published reports alleging that Walliams had been accused of sexual misconduct by several women.

The Met said that the allegations being investigated are separate from those reported by ITV and the Guardian, but as "part of their investigation, detectives are also proactively reviewing that reporting to establish whether there is any evidence of offences".

When those allegations were first reported, Walliams said he was "not a sexual predator" and had not "broken the law".

In a statement released on Friday, the Met said it had "received a number of allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving a man now in his 50s".

"Those who have come forward are being supported by specialist officers," the statement added.

Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney said: "We would encourage anyone who has been the victim of a sexual offence to come forward and speak to us, no matter when it happened.

"We know reporting allegations of this nature can be daunting, but specialist officers are on hand to provide support, answer questions and guide you through the process."

Allegations against the entertainer and children's author were published after he lost a legal bid to stop claims against him being made public by the media.

Some of the women in the investigation accused Walliams of "grooming" them when they were teenagers.

One now characterises her alleged encounter with Walliams at 15 years old as a "sexual assault". Walliams strongly denied he had any sexual contact with the girl.

He said he rejected any allegations of criminal activity and that he has never engaged in the grooming of young women.

The Guardian and ITV News said that several of the women, who do not know one another, allege they were targets of unwanted sexual advances from Walliams.

The investigation also claimed Walliams had a sexual relationship with at least one junior employee at publisher HarperCollins, and pursued another.

Other women alleged inappropriate behaviour at ITV's Britain's Got Talent, such as inviting girls and young women to his dressing room.

In a letter addressed to journalists working on the ITV and Guardian investigation, Walliams wrote: "Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.

"I realise I did not always take people's feelings properly into account. That is something I regret.

"And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did."

He added: "I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me."

Walliams shot to fame in the early 2000s with BBC sketch comedy Little Britain, served as a judge on ITV's Britain's Got Talent and launched a best-selling series of children's books.

articles.title: Car bombings in Russia kill military officer, injure ex-Ukraine PM adviser
articles.summary: Moscow blames Kyiv for a series of car bombings that have targeted people linked to the war with Ukraine.
articles.body:
A car bombing in Moscow has critically injured an adviser to Ukraine’s former prime minister a day after a similar attack killed a military officer in St Petersburg.

The explosion on Friday was the latest in a series of bombings and shootings that have targeted people involved in the fighting in Ukraine. Moscow has blamed Kyiv for the attacks.

The Moscow explosion struck a car driven by Sergei Zavorotnyi, who previously worked as an adviser to former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov, according to Russia’s Investigative Committee.

Zavorotnyi was hospitalised with injuries, the committee added. It did not identify possible suspects pending a criminal inquiry.

Azarov served as prime minister under Ukraine’s Moscow-friendly President Viktor Yanukovych, who was forced from office by protesters and fled to Russia in February 2014.

Azarov, who also lives in Russia, told state-run TV that he was “shocked” by the attack that left his former adviser critically injured. He said he believes Zavorotnyi was targeted because of his criticism of the Ukrainian government.

Zavorotnyi. 72, had worked as a journalist for Russia’s daily Komsomolskaya Pravda before becoming Azarov’s adviser. He wrote a book about Yanukovych’s ouster and ran an online outlet critical of Ukrainian authorities.

Russia’s REN TV channel said he lost his left arm, suffered multiple other injuries and was in a coma after the explosion.

Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova, reporting from Moscow, said an explosive device was reportedly planted under the man’s car and detonated remotely as he was driving on Friday.

“The investigative committee has already launched a criminal case into this explosion,” she said.

A day earlier, in St Petersburg, a military serviceman was killed by a bomb in his vehicle, according to Russia’s Investigative Committee. It did not identify the victim or say who could be behind the bombing.

The Fontanka news outlet said Thursday’s victim was a colonel, while other Russian online media said the victim was a senior air force officer.

Shapovalova said preliminary reports indicated that the victim was a military serviceman, rather than a colonel of the Russian Air Force.

Like the attack on Friday, he was also driving the car when the bomb went off, she added.

“In both cases an explosive device was triggered remotely, and it was planted under their car,” Shapovalova said. “Here in Russia, all the attacks are considered to be orchestrated by the Ukrainian side.”

Ukrainian authorities have not commented on either bombing.

articles.title: Fort Worth Zoo hatched a record eight critically endangered gharial crocodiles in one season, increasing its juvenile population from 5 to 13
articles.summary: Fort Worth Zoo in Texas has recorded a major milestone in its conservation efforts after successfully hatching 8 critically endangered gharial crocodiles
articles.body: Fort Worth Zoo in Texas has recorded a major milestone in its conservation efforts after successfully hatching 8 critically endangered gharial crocodiles in a single season. The achievement has increased the zoo’s juvenile gharial population from 5 to 13, marking its most successful breeding season for the species so far. According to the zoo’s September 9, 2026, announcement, the hatchings also represent the fourth consecutive year of successful reproduction, highlighting the institution’s growing experience in protecting one of the world’s most threatened crocodilian species.Fort Worth Zoo hatches eight critically endangered gharial crocodilesThe Fort Worth Zoo announced that eight gharial crocodiles hatched between June 3 and June 26, 2026. According to its official announcement, the new arrivals increased the zoo’s juvenile gharial population from 5 to 13, representing a substantial addition to its existing group.The zoo described the achievement as a record-breaking breeding season and another important step in its long-running conservation programme. It also maintained its position as the only institution in North America to have produced multiple offspring of this critically endangered species and successfully repeated the achievement over consecutive years.The announcement explained that the hatchlings came from egg clutches representing the genetic material of two different females. This is significant because maintaining genetic diversity is an important part of building a healthier population of animals under human care.How has the zoo improved its gharial breeding programmeThe latest breeding success follows more than 15 years of dedicated work at Fort Worth Zoo to reproduce gharials, increase their population and diversify their gene pool.According to the zoo, its team has gradually refined breeding, incubation and hatchling care practices over several years. This season, staff introduced additional heated nesting logs in the adult gharials’ outdoor habitat and continued making careful adjustments to egg incubator temperatures.Temperature management is particularly important for reptiles because incubation conditions can influence the sex of offspring. The zoo explained that experts could not identify a single change responsible for the unusually successful season. Instead, they believe the combined effect of improvements made over time has contributed to better results.Vicky Poole, associate curator of ectotherms at Fort Worth Zoo, said each successful hatching provides another opportunity for the team to improve its techniques and develop a deeper understanding of the species. The knowledge gained through these efforts can also be shared with conservation partners elsewhere in the world.What makes the gharial breeding habitat importantFort Worth Zoo's adult gharial habitat was specifically designed to encourage breeding and support the animals' needs. The habitat, located outside the Museum of Living Art, was developed in 2010 with several features intended to improve breeding conditions.These include controlled water temperatures, gently sloping waterfronts that allow gharials to move between wet and dry areas, and heat coils beneath the sand to maintain suitable temperatures for egg-laying.The design takes account of the gharial's physical characteristics, including its relatively short legs, which make access to different parts of its habitat important.The zoo's continued breeding success suggests that habitat design, careful egg incubation and years of accumulated experience have become central to its conservation work.Why are gharials critically endangeredGharials are among the most distinctive crocodilian species, recognisable by their long, narrow snouts. Their specialised jaws make them particularly well suited to catching fish, while their streamlined bodies and swimming abilities allow them to spend much of their lives in water. But the species faces serious threats in its natural environment.Fort Worth Zoo identifies habitat destruction, pollution and river fragmentation among the principal challenges affecting gharial survival. These pressures make it increasingly difficult for the animals to thrive in their native river systems.The Zoological Association of America also highlighted the species' endangered status in its July 2025 report on the zoo's earlier breeding achievement. That report explained how offspring from a female whose genes had not previously been represented among hatchlings helped diversify the genetic pool of gharials in managed care.The conservation value of successful breeding therefore extends beyond increasing the number of animals. It also involves preserving genetic diversity that could help support the species' future.How are the gharial hatchlings being cared forThe 8 hatchlings from the 2026 season are currently being kept behind the scenes at Fort Worth Zoo, where staff can closely monitor their growth and development.The zoo said visitors could already see juvenile gharials from previous breeding seasons in the indoor habitat at its Museum of Living Art, also known as MOLA. The facility is the only location in North America where visitors can observe juveniles of this critically endangered species.The zoo's earlier breeding achievements have also helped establish a longer record of success. A July 2025 report by the Zoological Association of America documented two gharial hatchlings that year, following successful hatchings in 2023 and 2024. It described the achievement as the first consecutive series of successful gharial hatchings in North America.Breeding success alone cannot resolve the threats gharials face in their natural habitats, maintaining a growing and genetically diverse population under managed care remains an important part of conservation efforts.You use AI every day. articles.title: The quarterback market in college football is out of control, and Kamario Taylor is just the beginning
articles.summary: Kamario Taylor's reported $7.5 million NIL deal to stay at Mississippi State signals a quarterback market that shows no signs of slowing down.
articles.body: Inflation is getting out of control, and I'm not talking about prices at the supermarket. That's right, folks. If you've been paying attention, the market for a quarterback in college football continues to go through the roof, and this week it seems another domino has fallen in the great signal caller NIL saga. Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor is now the new recipient of a $7.5 million deal to stay in Starkville, with reports that the number could climb north of $9 million with incentives. MISSISSIPPI STATE’S KAMARIO TAYLOR FINALIZING A REPORTED $7.5 MILLION DEAL, IN WILD COLLEGE FOOTBALL MOVE Let's get this out of the way right now: I'm happy for Taylor and for Mississippi State fans. The Bulldogs haven't had much to cheer about since the turn of the decade, and Taylor looks like one of the brightest young passers in the country, albeit with a limited sample size to his name. KIRBY SMART CLARIFIES COMMENTS AFTER TAKING SHOT AT HOW MUCH COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYERS ARE MAKING I also understand why MSU felt like they needed to do this. With some of the transfer portal sharks circling and the market for quarterbacks only getting more competitive, it was smart for the program to lock down someone scouts believe will be a top-tier draft pick whenever he decides to leave. But there's that pesky "market" word rearing its ugly head. We've seen it in the NFL, where mediocre quarterbacks with thin resumes are given massive deals based solely on the fact that they were either high draft picks that flashed potential or are essentially warm bodies. I won't name names, but a certain South Florida franchise that I root for is still paying for their quarterback to ride the pine with another team about 650 miles to the north. This will absolutely start happening in college, though some would argue it already has. BIG MONEY, BIGGER DISASTER: MINNESOTA EXPOSES MICHIGAN AS WOLVERINES ARE LATEST EXAMPLE OF WASTED NIL FUNDS Remember when Texas Tech paid Brendan Sorsby somewhere in the neighborhood of $5-6 million because he had a solid season with Cincinnati? That didn't work out for the Red Raiders, and that was due to issues entirely off the field. How about when Tennessee paid Nico Iamaleava a reported $8 million (roughly $2.4 million a season) out of high school, only for him to heed the words of the Pet Shop Boys and "Go West" to UCLA? That happened in 2022, when NIL was in its infancy, so you know those numbers are only going to trend upwards. I mean no offense to Kamario Taylor, who by all accounts is a brilliant quarterback when healthy, but he's thrown a total of 236 pass attempts in his career and hasn't even played a whole season of football. Imagine what a player like Keelon Russell will command if he continues to have the season he's having with Alabama. WHICH TEAMS HAVE THE MOST VALUABLE COLLEGE FOOTBALL ROSTERS HEADING INTO 2026 SEASON? If the Crimson Tide end up winning an SEC Championship, their quarterback could ask for a small private island, and the boosters would either have to capitulate or watch him go to Miami or Texas A&M for a similarly hefty fee. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP These rosters will continue to ratchet up in price. Just a few seasons ago, Ryan Day publicly pleaded with his booster base, saying he needed $20 million to fund a championship roster. Today, that number would get you laughed out of the room at most competitive, Power 4 programs. I don't know where the sport is headed from here, but one thing is for sure, this influx of money isn't slowing down any time soon. The sport is generating a ton of revenue and the players hold all the power. Salary caps and collective bargaining agreements are all being quietly suggested, but for now, college football is still operating with a "wild west" format. Whether or not that's sustainable at this pace remains to be seen.

articles.title: Two Australian reality TV judges bought two abandoned Sicilian houses for €1 each;  they discovered that part of a centuries-old building was structurally unsafe and transformed the properties into a four-level home, now listed for €195,000
articles.summary: Shaynna Blaze and Darren Palmer, the two judges and interior designers on The Block, have listed the Sicilian house they rebuilt for Channel Nine’s 1 Euro
articles.body: Shaynna Blaze and Darren Palmer, the two judges and interior designers on The Block, have listed the Sicilian house they rebuilt for Channel Nine’s 1 Euro House. The fully furnished property in Castronovo di Sicilia has an asking price of €195,000 (A$316,000), according to a report by the Herald Sun.The €1 Sicilian housesBlaze and Palmer each bought a derelict house for €1 in the hill town, both of which had stood empty for decades. They didn’t really get the chance to see the properties before the purchase. The buildings were already crumbling when they bought them. They “spent a season putting their own reputations on the line to bring it back to life”, according to the listing on TIPCo.Palmer’s first reaction to the show’s teaser was blunt: “This is so much worse than I thought!” The house dates back 400 to 500 years. Part of it was structurally unsound and had to be demolished. Rather than leave the gap empty, the designers turned that section into an open-air, Mediterranean-style walled garden. The garden now gives the home a private outdoor space, which is rare in a historic village centre.Palmer bought the second house next door, and the pair combined both properties into a single four-level home. According to the listing, it is now a two-bedroom, two-bathroom property. It also comes with a powder room, a garage and an internal area of about 160 square metres, measured from the architect’s plans rather than a survey.Inside the houseBy the time the pair bought the properties, half of the original structure had to go. However, the designers ensured that its roots remained intact. “What rose in its place is a home that keeps the soul of an old Sicilian village house (exposed stone, hidden arches, timber beams, reclaimed tiles) and pairs it with the warmth and ease of contemporary Australian design”, the listing says.Much of the interior was created with the help of Sicilian craftspeople. Handmade tiles, local marble and artisan ceramics went into the kitchen and bathrooms. The summer room has stone walls, poured concrete floors and restored vintage furniture, while the top floor has a terrace bar. The breathtaking chandelier came from a shop in Palermo, where Blaze bargained the price down from €170 to €150.The house is being sold fully furnished, which means buyers will get what they see in the pictures shared in the listing. This includes furniture, lighting, artworks, soft furnishings and kitchen equipment.Castronovo di Sicilia sits in the Sicani Mountains, roughly halfway between Palermo and Agrigento. It is a hill town of stone lanes and church bell towers, quiet enough for life to move at its own pace. Palermo is about an hour away by car, as are Agrigento and the coast, while the airport is around 80 minutes away. Shops, bars and a pharmacy are within the town itself. “It is quiet, unhurried and still very much lived in, with a piazza where everyone knows each other. It’s the kind of place the series fell in love with”, the listing says.Blaze also announced the sale on Instagram. She said the price would buy a one-bedroom apartment in a high-rise in an Australian capital city, while the Sicilian house offers outdoor space, parking and more living area. “If you have loved watching this and want to live the Sicilian dream, well, this is your chance”, she said in the video. She also credited the renovation to the two of them. “I’m so proud of what Darren and I have been able to achieve with our minimal budget, our timeline, our lack of help.”Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Naidu turns Araku coffee, AP cocoa into investment pitch
articles.summary: Naidu pitches Araku coffee, AP cocoa to UAE minister at CII Summit; says data centres can use Godavari water and 80% renewables; launches Swayam AP brand.
articles.body: Coffee, chocolates and investmentsChief minister N Chandrababu Naidu turned a casual exchange over coffee and chocolates into an investment pitch during his interaction with UAE minister of economy and tourism Abdulla bin Touq Al Marri ahead of CII Partnership Summit. Naidu offered him Araku coffee and said he wanted the UAE minister to remember Andhra Pradesh whenever he had a cup and consider investing in the state. The UAE minister responded by offering chocolates from his country. Naidu quickly pointed out that cocoa used in the chocolates was grown in Andhra Pradesh and offered to supply it. He also suggested setting up a chocolate manufacturing unit in the state.Naidu, Lokesh dispel data centre concernsConcerns over the environmental impact and water consumption of data centres came up during the various sessions at the summit. Chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu said there is no need for concern over water use, as Andhra Pradesh could bring 100 TMC of Godavari water to Visakhapatnam through the Polavaram left canal. He said nearly 3,000 TMC of Godavari water flows into the sea every year. The water could meet the needs of data centres as well as drinking, agriculture and industry, he said. IT minister Nara Lokesh said data centres in the state would be required to use 80% renewable energy.Swayam AP for womenThe Andhra Pradesh govt announced plans to launch a dedicated brand, Swayam AP, to take products made by women self-help groups to international markets. The initiative aims to give women entrepreneurs wider market access and improve their business opportunities. Of the 25 lakh MSMEs in the state, around 11 lakh are owned by women, according to the information shared at the summit. Coastal women are being trained in seaweed cultivation and millet-based cooking to create additional livelihood opportunities.Summit opens to public from todayThe industrial exhibitions and pavilions set up at Andhra University engineering college grounds as part of CII Partnership Summit will be open to the public on Saturday, Nov 14. The MSME and Andhra Pradesh pavilions, along with industrial exhibition galleries, will be accessible to visitors. The district administration said the initiative would give people an opportunity to see the state’s industrial development initiatives, emerging investment opportunities, employment prospects and innovations. It would also help aspiring entrepreneurs understand the support available to start and develop businesses.Vizag city gets summit spotlight for cleanlinessVisakhapatnam’s cleanliness and recent Swachh awards found mention in the speeches of several delegates at CII Partnership Summit, including chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu. The city received a makeover ahead of the two-day event, as GVMC took up road repairs, median beautification, landscaping and improvements along the beach stretch. The civic works are aimed at improving the city’s appearance and infrastructure before the arrival of delegates from India and abroad. articles.title: Black Mississippians celebrate a victory almost no one saw coming
articles.summary: Scott Colom is the first black man to sit in the Senate for Mississippi in 145 years.
articles.body:
Dozens of people filled a tiny room inside the historic Masonic Lodge Hall in Jackson, Mississippi, on Wednesday, waiting to hear whether Scott Colom would become the state's next US Senator.

The 70-year-old building is the permanent residence of the NAACP's state headquarters, where civil rights leaders, many of them there that night, worked for decades to create this moment.

When a large speaker blared the news of Colom's win, it ended a long, anxious wait for results that came over a week after election day. The room exploded with emotion.

"Yes sir," one man yelled, dropping to the ground and moving his arms and legs as if to make a snow angel on the carpet floor.

Colom's victory is the first win for Democrats in the seat in more than 40 years. And that candidate, who was elected for the final time in 1982, supported segregation.

It is also the first time a black politician has held the seat since 1881. Mississippi's population is almost 40% black, which is a larger share of the electorate than any other state.

Republicans have, following a ruling by the US Supreme Court overturning parts of the Voting Rights Act, made moves to reduce the number of majority-black districts, which many experts say weakens black voting power. It is partly due to this backdrop that Colom's victory resonated with many.

"All the stories that my father used to tell me about him growing up here in Jackson, and all the hardships and unjust treatment that he faced. And having experienced some of that myself, it's hard to put it into words what this moment means for us," Cedric Haynes said.

"Whoever thought this day would have come."

People cheered, hugged, kissed and cried, celebrating the achievement.

"I think it is special. It is holy, and it something different," Charles Taylor, executive director of the NAACP's Mississippi branch, said.

Taylor now sits in the same office that was once occupied by Medgar Evers, a black WWII veteran and civil rights activist who was killed by an assassin's bullet in Mississippi, in 1963, in part for his effort to register black Americans to vote.

To win in the Magnolia State, Colom has not only had to overcome the state's racial history, but defy its political gravity. Mississippi has long been a Republican stronghold. Donald Trump won re-election to the presidency here by over 22 points, just two years go.

In the early days of the midterm election season, which ultimately ended in Democrats flipping a record number of seats in Congress, not even the party's wildest ambitions included a Mississippi victory.

Two days after election day, with a lead of only a few hundred votes, Colom said the national party had long given up on the state.

"I've been in Mississippi for 15 years," Colom told NBC News on 5 November. "Most of the time Democrats have conceded the state."

He continued: "What you're saying is, I don't care enough about those voters."

But Colom won anyways, despite having a roughly $2m campaign donation deficit compared to the Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith, according to the most recent FEC records.

The tide turned for Colom and Democrats, with help from massive grassroots campaigning and organising.

The NAACP said it knocked on more than 150,000 doors across the state and made stops at over 2,500 churches in the lead-up to the election - compared to 70,000 doors and 500 churches in the last election. The NAACP is non-partisan and did not favour a candidate - but exit polls showed 91% of black voters in Mississippi backed Colom.

About 300,000 more voters showed up to Mississippi's polls in 2026, compared to the last mid-term's in 2022.

His victory against nearly impossible odds was also bolstered by a strong showing from young voters, corralled by organisations like Mississippi Votes who showed up on college campuses across the state to encourage voter registration.

Arekia Bennett-Scott, executive director of Mississippi Votes, said over 600 students from Jackson State University, a local historically black college, voted this midterm election – trumping the figure of roughly 100 Jackson State students who voted during the last midterm.

The night of Colom's win, a group of drum majors from Jackson State's historic marching band, the Sonic Boom of the South, were heading into the locker room after practice, relishing their part in making history.

"I'm absolutely ecstatic. I'm overly excited that (Colom) won," drum major Jared Thompson said. "This is one of the first elections that I voted on as a young adult."

"And, you know, we hear a lot of this rhetoric that, 'oh my vote doesn't matter,'" he continued. "Tonight was proof, without a shadow of a doubt, that your vote matters."

Another major factor that contributed to Colom's success was a national backlash against the Republican party, driven by a rise in the cost of living linked to Trump policies, which caused several other Republican fortresses to fall on election night, including Texas, Kansas, and Iowa.

Hyde-Smith was also criticised for running a lackluster campaign, where she made very few public appearances. Meanwhile, Colom visited each of Mississippi's 82 counties, including a five-day campaign called the Where's Cindy Tour.

After the Republican recommended people pick another protein if the cost of beef was too high, Colom released an attack ad that went viral, encouraging voters to "pick another senator".

At his victory speech, on the grounds of the historically black university Tougaloo College on Wednesday evening, hundreds of supporters gathered, many holding signs that said: "Picked another Senator."

A member of the Tougaloo Concert Choir sang the US National Anthem. Colom's two daughters, Gwendolyn and Brooklyn, aged 9 and 8, respectively, then led a recital of the Pledge of Allegiance, as hands were held over hearts.

After Colom's wife, Nadia, took the stage, he emerged between a narrow opening in a thicket of supporters to address the public as senator-elect for the very first time.

In his opening remarks, he cited Medgar Evers, the black veteran who was assassinated for trying to help black Americans register to vote.

"He had faith that Mississippi could make progress," Colom said.

"For months and months, I've been telling everybody, everywhere I go, that we're gonna win this election," he continued. "Every time I said it, I pointed out that people were going to give me too much credit for it because it's not something that I did, y'all. It's something that we did."

"All I did was have the courage to imagine a night like this."

With additional reporting from Kyla Herrmannsen

articles.title: Microsoft outage 'stark reminder' of how much we rely on tech
articles.summary: Microsoft has apologised for the issue, which it said was due to a technical failure.
articles.body:
A critical Microsoft outage lasting more than 22 hours has raised questions about how heavily vital services rely on a handful of major tech firms.

The disruption, which affected Microsoft 365 services such as Outlook, was caused by routine automated checks that took some servers offline, overloading the remaining ones with traffic.

The recovery took nearly a full day while engineers gradually restored services, highlighting how embedded the tech giant's services are in modern society.

Flora Hamilton, executive director of the Small Business Charter, said the outage was a "stark reminder" of how much firms "rely on digital systems" - like Microsoft Outlook - "to keep their operations running".

"For many small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), access to email is fundamental to everything from communicating with customers and suppliers to generating income," she said.

The disruption was not just confined to businesses, but also affected organisations and public institutions around the world.

Around 430 million people globally use Microsoft 365, and issues were reported across more than 70 countries.

The fallout from the outage had a wide-ranging effect , knocking out email systems for the US House of Representatives and Australian intelligence agencies, as well as disrupting court systems in Singapore and airline support desks in India.

Microsoft has since apologised for the issue, which it said was due to a technical failure rather than a cyber-attack.

Walter Pasquarelli, an AI strategist, told the BBC that for governments, businesses and critical infrastructure, the outage had "put their vulnerabilities and dependence in plain sight".

"Looking ahead, as AI assistants are plugged into our email, calendars and files, a failure like this may spread even further," he said.

Microsoft says email queues 'approaching normal levels' after global outage hits Outlook and Teams users

Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies, said while these kinds of outages weren't unheard of, what was unusual was the time it took for Microsoft to recover from it.

A spokesperson for the US tech company said "given the scale of demand" it restored services gradually.

"While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration," a spokesperson said.

Orosz said the resulting upset showed "our reliance on a few large US corporations".

He said a solution for the future could be to split services per region to reduce the impact, something which already happens with Amazon's cloud computing service, AWS.

For now, Microsoft said it was reviewing what went wrong, with the findings expected to inform steps to prevent a similar disruption from happening again.
